source_text: Intellexisti quippe, parvulis nihil de suo merentibus, nequaquam posse sine damnatione corporum, crimen affigi; et ideo opus esse auxilio Manichaei, qui concupiscentiam carnis a Dei operibus excluderet, et tam nuptias quam ipsa corpora diabolo deputaret auctori.
pass_a_gloss: For you understood that a charge can by no means be fastened on little ones meriting nothing of their own, without condemnation of bodies; and therefore there is need of the help of Manichaeus, who would exclude the desire of the flesh from God's works, and would assign both marriages and the bodies themselves to the devil as author.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS nuptiae; Blaise Christian marriage as God's work
LS parvulus; Blaise infants as Julian's test case

pass_b_english: For you understood that a charge could never be fastened on infants, who have deserved nothing of their own, without condemning bodies. You therefore needed the help of Manichaeus, who excluded the desire of the flesh from God’s works and assigned both marriage and bodies themselves to the devil as their author.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
